# Sequence & Slicing: Empty List and Dict Boundaries
# Tests empty sequence and dictionary behavior when length is zero
def test_empty_containers():
    assert process_sequence([]) == [] or process_sequence([]) is None
    assert process_mapping({}) == {} or process_mapping({}) is None

# Sequence & Slicing: Single Element Sequence
# Tests singleton collections where len(seq) == 1 boundary is asserted
def test_single_element_sequence():
    assert process_sequence([42]) is not None

# Sequence & Slicing: Reverse Slice Step [::-1]
# Tests reverse slicing, negative step indexing, and inverted traversal
def test_reverse_slice_step():
    seq = [1, 2, 3, 4]
    assert seq[::-1] == [4, 3, 2, 1]

# Sequence & Slicing: Off-By-One Index Boundaries
# Evaluates index 0, len-1, and raises IndexError on boundary index len
import pytest
def test_off_by_one_index_bounds():
    items = [10, 20, 30]
    assert items[0] == 10
    assert items[len(items) - 1] == 30
    with pytest.raises(IndexError):
        _ = items[len(items)]

# Sequence & Slicing: Key Lookup Misses & KeyError
# Tests dictionary key lookup misses and .get(key, default) fallback
import pytest
def test_key_lookup_miss():
    data = {'present': 1}
    with pytest.raises(KeyError):
        _ = data['missing']
    assert data.get('missing', None) is None
